Task:
Read input.csv from the current directory. Its columns are unit (unit identifier), period (calendar period), y (outcome), x (endogenous regressor), and z (excluded instrument).

Estimate y responses at h=0,1,2 using 2SLS local projections. Each origin (unit,t) must have that same unit observed at calendar t-1,t,t+1,t+2. Use this common sample for every horizon. For each h, regress y_(t+h) on endogenous x_t, y_(t-1), unit fixed effects, and origin-period fixed effects. Include an intercept and omit one category from each fixed-effect set. The only excluded instrument is z_t. All included exogenous regressors instrument themselves. Report x coefficients as lp_h0,lp_h1,lp_h2. Do not treat adjacent stored rows as adjacent calendar periods. The sample count is the number of retained origin rows.

Report these terms: lp_h0, lp_h1, lp_h2. Return each requested number as an estimate. Standard errors are not requested. Set se to null. Set n_obs to 481, the sample count defined above. Print one line per estimate using this format. Use the sample count specified in the task. Report at least eight significant digits. Each requested uncertainty measure is a separate estimate term. Use exact integers for declared count targets.
ANSWER: lp_h0 estimate=<number> se=NA n_obs=<integer>
ANSWER: lp_h1 estimate=<number> se=NA n_obs=<integer>
ANSWER: lp_h2 estimate=<number> se=NA n_obs=<integer>

Write one self-contained Stata script. The evaluator runs it with the supplied CSV files in its working directory.
Act only as a code generator. Do not use tools, inspect files, or execute code.
Return exactly one fenced stata code block and nothing else.
